speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; to begin my assessment, how long has this breathing difficulty been occurring, and was there any exposure to amniotic fluid or meconium during delivery? REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: pH: 7.30 (slightly acidic), PaCO2: 50 mm Hg (elevated), PaO2: 60 mm Hg (reduced), HCO3-: 24 mEq/L, Base_Excess: -5

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Meconium Aspiration Syndrome.
Your symptoms of tachypnea, retractions, and cyanosis are classic for respiratory distress in a newborn, but a urinary tract infection would not present with these specific respiratory findings; I need to confirm if there was meconium staining of the amniotic fluid or if you were born prematurely. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.
